rooms.1325: The gold-leaved trees stop short here at a line of white stones, set into the moss at even paces as if someone once marked where the light should end. Beyond the stones to the east the Old Forest begins at once, a wall of black-trunked oaks hung with grey lichen and filled with a breathless gloom. The bright margin runs north toward a corner of the Radiant Forest and south along the line of stones. Behind you the canopy glows a soft, unhurried yellow.
rooms.1334: A great gold-leaved tree has fallen across the border here, its roots torn up out of the radiant wood and its crown sprawled east among the dark trunks of the Old Forest. The leaves on this side of the line still shine like new coin, while those beyond it have curled brown and dead. The margin of the forest runs north and south, and west the golden trees stand close and calm. A smell of wet bark and torn earth hangs about the upturned roots.
rooms.1350: This is the last corner of the radiant wood, and the Old Forest presses against it from the east and the south alike, its gnarled trunks wrapped in ivy and its floor lost in shadow. A thicket of holly grows along the boundary, dark leaves glossy against the pale gold overhead. Cold mist seeps between the stems and thins away to nothing a few paces inside the light. The bright margin of the forest leads north and west from here.
rooms.1349: Brambles heavy with blackberries tangle along the southern edge of the golden wood, and a gap has been trampled through them where some large beast has pushed its way south into the Old Forest. Beyond the gap the ground drops into a gloom of roots and nettles. The edge runs on east to a corner of the wood and west beneath arching boughs, while north the radiant trees open around a still pool. Birdsong drifts down from the canopy, untroubled by the darkness so close by.
rooms.1345: A still pool lies in a hollow among the roots, so clear that the gold of the canopy seems to float on its surface like fallen leaves. Its banks are soft with moss and starred with tiny white flowers. A narrow glade opens to the north, the trees thin toward the forest's edge to the south, and a path of flattened grass leads west between the trunks. The light gathers on the water here and lingers long after it should have faded.
rooms.1341: The trees close in on three sides of this small glade, leaving only the way south open. White anemones carpet the ground so thickly that there is hardly room to set a foot between them. At the far end someone has bent a row of young saplings together and bound their tops with grass, making a living bower just tall enough to sit beneath. Light falls through the leaves in soft gold shafts that barely move.
rooms.1344: Two rows of tall, straight trees stand here as evenly spaced as the pillars of a temple, their silver trunks rising without a branch for twenty feet before they break into crowns of pale gold. Leaves drift down between them so slowly that they seem to hang in the air. The avenue runs east toward a still pool and west deeper into the wood. Your footsteps make no sound at all on the deep leaf litter.
rooms.1343: A boulder furred with green moss squats among the roots here, and from a crack at its foot a spring wells up and spills away in a thread of bright water. Several faint paths meet beside it, as though everyone who passes stops to drink. One runs east along an avenue of tall trunks, another west into a leaf-filled hollow, and a third south toward the dark line of the forest's edge. The water tastes cold and faintly of stone.
rooms.1347: A huge, hollow oak of the Old Forest leans over the border from the south, its black limbs reaching into the light like a hand stretched toward a fire. Beneath it a ring of grey toadstools has sprung up on the very line where gold leaves give way to brown. The edge runs east and west, and north a path winds back among the radiant trees toward a mossy spring. The air grows colder with every step toward the oak.
rooms.1348: A shallow stream slips out from under the golden trees here and runs south into the Old Forest, and you can watch its water change as it goes, bright and chattering on this side, dark and silent beyond. A line of stepping stones crosses it just short of the boundary. Ferns crowd both banks, green and lush here and blackened further on. The forest's edge continues east and west along the border.
rooms.1346: A slender pillar of white stone stands at this corner of the radiant wood, cracked and leaning, with a single leaf carved near its top. The Old Forest crowds up to it from the south and the west, a dark mass of yew and oak whose shadows stop at the foot of the pillar as if they dare go no further. Along the bright margin the way runs north and east. Bindweed has wound its pale trumpets around the base of the stone.
rooms.1335: To the west stands a wall of dark firs, the first trees of the Old Forest, so close-set that their lower branches have died grey and brittle in the gloom. The soft moss underfoot gives way to a crust of brown needles right at the boundary. A cold breath of air comes out of the firs, smelling of resin and old rot. The golden margin leads north and south, and east the radiant trees open invitingly.
rooms.1326: A great hollow stump stands at the boundary, its jagged rim taller than a man and its inside packed with gold leaves blown in from the radiant wood. Beside it a narrow game trail slips west into the Old Forest, where brambles close over it within a dozen paces. The edge of the golden trees runs north and south. Eastward the wood opens beneath the crown of a tree so vast that it dwarfs every other.
rooms.1319: An old earth bank runs along the border here, with a ditch on its far side where the Old Forest begins. Ivy has swallowed the bank completely and climbs the first dark trunks to the west as though trying to drag them down. On this side the gold-leaved trees grow right up to the bank and lean slightly away from it. The margin leads north to a corner of the wood and south along the bank.
rooms.1309: Two ancient yews of the Old Forest stand guard at this corner, one to the north and one to the west, their red trunks twisted like rope and their needles so dark they look black. Between them the golden light of the radiant wood grows thin and grey. A post of grey stone stands at the very corner, topped by an empty iron cage where a lantern once hung to mark the border. The bright margin runs east and south from here.
rooms.1310: Overhead the canopy changes abruptly, pale gold leaves meeting the dark, heavy crowns of the Old Forest along a line as sharp as a seam. Roots of both kinds of tree knot together underfoot and make the going slow. The Old Forest lies north, the radiant margin runs east and west, and south a path leads in beneath the golden boughs. Somewhere in the dark wood a branch creaks with no wind to move it.
rooms.1314: A long fallen log lies half sunk in the moss here, so old that ferns and tiny saplings sprout along its back. Bluebells crowd the ground around it in a haze of blue beneath the gold. Paths lead north to the edge of the wood, east into a nook among hazels and south into a ring of tall ferns. The air smells green and sweet, like crushed stems after rain.
rooms.1315: Hazel bushes close around this quiet nook on every side but the west. Their roots have been coaxed, over many years, into the shape of a low bench, smooth and polished from use, set facing a gap in the leaves where the light pours through. Cobnuts hang in pale green clusters above it. It is the kind of place where someone might sit for a whole afternoon and never notice the time passing.
rooms.1320: Tall ferns grow in a ring here, higher than your head, enclosing a circle of short turf like the walls of a green room. In the middle sits a shallow basin of grey stone, filled with rainwater in which a few gold leaves turn slowly. There is no way through the ferns except the path back north. The quiet is so complete that you can hear the drip of dew from the fronds.
rooms.1327: The ground here heaves up in long ridges where the roots of a vast tree run beneath it, some of them thicker than a horse's body. North, the trunk itself rises like a grey cliff, its crown lost in a blaze of gold far above. Narrower ways lead east and south between the lesser trees, and west the light thins toward the edge of the wood. Moss fills every crease between the roots.
rooms.1321: A tree of impossible size rises here, its trunk wider than a cottage and its bark grey and smooth as old silver. A stair has been shaped out of the living wood, spiralling up around the trunk toward the hidden halls of Elvandar, but a gate of woven silver branches closes its lowest step and will not open. Paths leave the roots to the north, east, south and west. Gold light rains down from the canopy far overhead.
rooms.1322: The great tree's trunk bulges out of the ground just west of here, so broad that it fills half the view. Smaller gold-leaved trees crowd around it like children at their mother's skirts, and the leaves they drop lie thick and round as coins. Paths lead north past a lone silver birch, east among the trees and south toward a crossing of deer trails. A faint, sweet scent drifts down from blossoms high above.
rooms.1316: A single silver birch grows among the gold-leaved trees here, white and slender, its bark peeling in papery curls and pocked with the neat round holes of woodpeckers. It looks out of place, like a guest who has wandered into the wrong house. The way bends here, running east under low boughs and south toward a towering trunk. The leaf litter is deep and dry and rustles at every step.
rooms.1317: Honeysuckle climbs the trunks here and hangs in sweet-smelling curtains from the lower branches, its cream and yellow flowers almost the colour of the light. North, the trees thin toward the edge of the radiant wood, where darker boughs show beyond. A path winds east toward a hidden dell and west past a lone white birch. The scent of the flowers is heavy enough to make you drowsy.
rooms.1318: This hidden dell lies below the level of the surrounding wood, its sides steep with moss and roots, and the only easy way out is the path climbing back west. At its bottom stands the statue of a slender figure in a long robe, holding up a lamp of carved stone. Moss has grown over her shoulders like a shawl, but her face is still clear and calm. The light in the dell is brighter than anywhere around it, and seems to come from the lamp.
rooms.1323: A path of flat white stones has been laid here between two of the great trees, each stone sunk level with the moss and worn hollow in the middle by countless soft footsteps. East the stones lead to the roots of one giant, and west they run back toward the other. Lesser trees line the way, their gold leaves meeting overhead. The stones are cool underfoot even where the light falls full on them.
rooms.1324: Another of the giant trees stands here, its roots arching out of the earth in great loops that you could walk beneath without stooping. A stair winds up the trunk toward the high halls of the elves, but its lowest flight ends well above the ground, and whatever ladder once reached it has been drawn up. Ways lead north into a sunken dell, east toward the edge of the wood, south to a stony brook and west along a path of white stones.
rooms.1330: A quick brook crosses the path here, running clear over gold-flecked pebbles, and a little bridge of three silver-grey planks, joined without a single nail, spans it. North, the roots of a giant tree loop out of the ground beyond the water, and south the path climbs gently into a clearing ringed with birches. Water-mint grows along the banks, and its smell rises sharp and clean when you brush against it.
rooms.1333: Seven white birches stand in a perfect circle here, too evenly placed to have grown that way by chance, and the clearing they enclose is carpeted with short, springy turf. Gold-leaved trees rise all around beyond them. Ways lead north to a brook, east to the margin of the wood, west under a woven arch and south toward the vast trunk of yet another great tree. Even the wind seems to step softly in this place.
rooms.1340: The great tree here has split near its base into two vast trunks that lean apart and then grow together again far overhead, leaving a tall cleft between them. A stair once climbed up through the cleft toward Elvandar, but a curtain of ivy and wild rose has grown over its lower steps, so thick and thorny that the way up is closed. Paths lead off north, east, south and west among the roots. Petals from the wild roses lie scattered on the moss.
rooms.1339: A sunny bank rises here, covered with wild thyme and small purple flowers that release a warm, peppery scent when crushed. The trees stand back from it a little, and the light lies on the bank like honey in a dish. East the cleft trunk of a great tree looms over the roots, north a path leads to a woven arch, and west the way continues under silver boughs. It is warm here, warmer than anywhere else in the wood.
rooms.1332: Two young trees have been trained toward each other here until their branches meet and twine together, forming an arch of living wood over the path. Their leaves are a deeper gold than those around them, and a few late blossoms still cling to the weave. Beyond the arch the way runs north to a spring among the clover, east into a circle of birches and south toward a sunny bank. The arch creaks softly whenever the wind passes through it.
rooms.1329: Clover and wild violets cover the ground here so thickly that the air is sweet with them, and a tiny spring trickles out from beneath a tree root to lose itself among the flowers. The trees grow close, their trunks banded with pale lichen. A path leads south beneath a woven arch, and another runs west to a crossing of trails. Gold leaves float in the little pools the spring has made.
rooms.1328: Several narrow deer trails cross here, pressed into the leaf litter by generations of hooves. One of the trunks beside the crossing has been rubbed bare and scored by antlers, the scratches glinting with golden sap. The trails lead north toward the flank of a giant tree, east to a spring among the clover and west toward a ridge of great roots. The ground is soft, and every track shows plainly.
rooms.1338: A waist-high stone stands beside the path here, pale and smooth, with a single rune carved deep into its face and filled with something that glints like gold. Moss has crept up its sides but leaves the rune clear. The path runs east to a warm, thyme-covered bank and west toward the glass lanterns of a great tree. The leaves overhead are so thick that the light comes through in shades of green and amber.
rooms.1337: Lanterns of pale glass hang from the lowest boughs of the colossal tree that rises here, and though no flame burns in any of them, still they glow. A stair spirals up the trunk toward the high dwellings of Elvandar, but its foot lies behind a door of living bark that has closed over the opening like a healed wound. Ways lead north between banks of fern, east past a carved stone, south toward a mossy spring and west among young trees.
rooms.1331: The way runs narrow here between two high banks thick with ferns, their fronds meeting overhead in a green tunnel shot through with gold. Water seeps from the banks and keeps the path soft and dark. North the tunnel opens toward a ridge of great roots, and south the glow of hanging lanterns shows where another giant tree stands. Your shoulders brush the cool fronds on either side.
rooms.1336: Where an old tree fell some years ago, a crowd of young saplings has sprung up to fight for the light, each one straight and slim with a crown of tender gold leaves. The trunk of the fallen giant still lies among them, soft with rot and bright with orange fungus. A path leads west to the edge of the wood, where dark firs stand beyond, and south into a hollow of drifted leaves. The saplings sway together in the slightest breeze.
rooms.1342: The ground dips into a broad hollow here, and the wind has filled it knee-deep with fallen leaves, gold on top and brown and soft beneath. Wading through them raises a dry, sweet smell like old parchment. The way climbs out north among young saplings and east toward a mossy boulder where a spring rises. The leaves shift and settle behind you, hiding your tracks almost at once.
rooms.8660: The Path of Light bends here, its paving of pale, close-fitted stones curving from north to east around the foot of a tall gold-leaved tree. Each stone holds a soft glow of its own, as though it had soaked up the daylight and could not quite let it go. Grass grows only along the edges of the paving, never between the stones. The trees stand back on either side, leaving the path open to a ribbon of bright sky.
rooms.8657: The Path of Light opens here into a round paved space where the ways meet, and in its centre the stones form a great mosaic of a rising sun in white and gold. The glow of the paving is strongest at the sun's heart. Ways lead north and west, both bending toward the same glade, while east the path runs on between tall trees and south it curves around a gold-leaved trunk. Leaves that fall on the mosaic never seem to stay there long.
rooms.8267: The carpenter's house is as much workshop as home, and its ground floor smells richly of oak shavings, glue and linseed oil. A long workbench scarred by years of chisels runs beneath the window, with saws, planes and augers hung in neat rows on pegs above it. Every stick of furniture is the carpenter's own work, from the carved settle by the hearth to the spindle-backed chairs. A grinning wooden face on the mantel looks suspiciously like the stonemason across the way. The door north leads out to the covered walk.
rooms.8263: Wheels in every stage of making fill this lofty shop: bare elm hubs stacked against the wall, felloes of ash clamped to a bending jig, and a finished cartwheel standing in the wheel pit to await its iron tyre. A great round tyring plate of stone lies near the back, blackened by the fires used to heat the iron. The floor is ankle-deep in curled shavings that crackle underfoot. The doorway north opens back onto the covered walk of the Old Temple Road.
rooms.8259: The footpath from the village ends here in a quiet clearing ringed by oaks and hollies. A round cottage with a mossy turf roof stands on the southern side, a thread of smoke rising from a hole at its peak and bunches of drying herbs hanging beneath its eaves. Mistletoe grows in pale clumps high in the oaks. North, the path leads back through the trees to the covered walk of Hommlet's Old Temple Road.
rooms.8260: The single round room of the cottage is warm and dim, lit by a fire of applewood in a ring of stones at its centre. Herbs, roots and dried flowers hang in hundreds of bunches from the rafters, filling the air with a dusty green scent, and shelves of clay jars line the curving wall. A sleeping pallet heaped with fleeces lies against one side, and a sprig of mistletoe is fixed above the door. The doorway north leads back out to the clearing.
rooms.8215: The common room of the Welcome Wench is long and low, with smoke-darkened beams, scrubbed floorboards and a stone fireplace big enough to roast an ox. Trestle tables and benches stand ready for the evening crowd. The bar opens to the west, an archway south leads to the kitchen, and a stout door in the north wall closes off a private dining room, while the front door gives east onto the village square. A staircase climbs toward the guest rooms, but a rope is stretched across its foot, and a trapdoor half hidden under a rag rug is bolted fast.
rooms.8216: This small, panelled room is kept for guests who can pay for privacy, and it shows: the oak table is polished to a mirror, the chairs are cushioned in faded red velvet, and a pair of brass candlesticks stands ready at either end. A narrow window of thick bottle-glass lets in a greenish, wavering light. Painted hunting scenes hang on the walls, and a small fire is laid ready in the grate. The door south leads back to the common room.
rooms.8217: Heat rolls out of the great hearth that fills one wall of the kitchen, where iron spits and a blackened cauldron hang over a bed of glowing coals. Copper pans gleam on their hooks, a long table is dusted with flour for the day's bread, and strings of onions and garlic dangle from the beams. A narrow stair climbs steeply to Gundigoot's own quarters, its door at the top locked fast, and a cellar hatch in the floor is held shut by a heavy padlock. The way north leads back to the common room.
rooms.8218: A long counter of dark oak, worn pale along its edge by countless elbows, runs the length of the bar, and behind it great casks of ale and cider rest on their sides in wooden cradles. Pewter tankards hang from hooks along a beam, each marked with the name or sign of a regular. The floor is strewn with sawdust that smells of spilled beer. An archway east opens back into the common room.
rooms.8211: The kitchen is the heart of this well-kept farmhouse, flagged with stone scrubbed almost white and warmed by a wide inglenook where a kettle sits on the hob. Smoked hams and flitches of bacon hang from hooks in the beams, and a butter churn stands ready in the corner. Everything is in its place, from the row of polished boots by the door to the sampler stitched with the farm's name above the fire. The door west leads back out to the Caravan Road.
rooms.8212: This farmhouse rivals its neighbour for comfort and makes a point of it: a bright woven carpet from some city market covers the floor of the front room, and pewter plates line a dresser carved with sheaves and sickles. A great stuffed pike glowers from a glass case above the fireplace, and a cushioned settle faces the hearth. Through the small, deep windows you can see a garden of beans and cabbages. The front door opens north onto the Caravan Road.
rooms.8157: A gap between the houses of the King's Road leads straight into a vast old tithe barn standing at the edge of the plains, its roof held up on oak posts as thick as trees. Hay is heaped high in the bays, and the mud nests of swallows crust the beams overhead. Great doors stand open to the north and south, and lower doors in the side walls lead east and west into the byres and sheds beyond. Dust hangs glittering in the shafts of light from the doorways.
rooms.8164: This long cattle byre has been built onto the end of the tithe barn, its stalls divided by worn wooden rails and its floor of beaten earth sloping toward a drain. Iron tethering rings are set into the wall at the height of a cow's head, and the place smells of dung and old straw, though the stalls stand empty. A door west leads back into the barn, and another south opens toward a low stone shelter. Small high windows let in a pale, dusty light.
rooms.8163: Shepherds have built this low shelter of fieldstone and turf where the farmland gives way to the open plains, and it is snug against the wind, if not against the smell of sheep. Hurdles of woven hazel lean against one wall, and a hearth of blackened stones holds the ashes of an old fire. Doors lead north into the byre, west into a neighbouring shed and south out onto the grassland. Tufts of greasy wool cling to every rough edge of the stone.
rooms.8162: Open grassland stretches away all around, flat and wind-combed, with nothing taller than a thistle to break it. North stands the low stone shelter of the shepherds, and south the blackened gable of a ruined cottage rises out of the grass, the first of the burnt houses of Townsbridge. The plains run on west beneath a wide, pale sky. The wind carries a faint, stale smell of old burning.
rooms.8161: This cottage on the edge of Townsbridge kept half its roof when the village burned, and charred rafters still hold up a sagging mat of thatch over one end of the room. Beneath it lie the remains of a family's life: a toppled dresser, a cold hearth, a stool scorched black. A doorway north opens onto the grassland, a passage south leads toward the road through the village, and a low doorway west gives onto a room so dark that nothing inside can be seen. The air tastes of soot.
rooms.3220: The road runs right through the gutted shell of what was once Townsbridge's coaching inn, passing beneath a broad carriage arch whose stones are still streaked with soot. Charred beams lie where the upper floor fell in, and a row of empty stalls lines one wall. West, the road leads through the blackened wall of a burnt shop, east it climbs toward the hills at the end of the plains road, and a doorway south opens into another ruin. A painted sign still hangs above the arch, burnt past reading.
rooms.8501: The plains road comes to an end here at the foot of rising hills, its last few yards marked by a squat milestone so worn it might be any old stone. North the ground climbs steeply toward the mountains, while east and south the long grass of the Meadow Thrithing spreads away, rippling silver in the wind. West the road runs back toward the burnt village of Townsbridge. Heather and gorse grow in clumps along the stony bank.
rooms.8502: The land begins to climb in earnest here, rough grass giving way to scree and outcrops of grey rock at the foot of the mountains. An old drystone wall runs along the slope, and set into it is a stout plank door, weathered silver, that opens west onto a small path along the mountains. North a steep track climbs toward a high plateau, east the meadow grass rolls away, and south lies the end of the plains road. The wind here has a cold edge to it.
rooms.8505: A windswept plateau of bare rock and thin, wiry grass spreads out here before the mountains, which rise in a sheer grey cliff close at hand. Cracks in the cliff face have been worn into a rough ladder of handholds and ledges that climbs up toward the cliffside high above. A cairn of piled stones marks the start of the climb. Far below, the meadow and the dark line of the woods lie spread out like a map, and the track leads back south down the slope.
rooms.1801: The Meadow Thrithing begins here where the stony slopes give way to grass, its long blades brushing your knees and rippling away in silver waves. West, the land rises toward the foot of the mountains, scattered with grey boulders that have tumbled from the heights. The meadow spreads east and south, bright with buttercups. A cold wind comes down off the slopes and sets the grass hissing.
rooms.1802: A lone hawthorn stands in the long grass here, bent almost double by the wind, its thorns hung with tufts of wool and coarse horsehair. Around it the grass has been trampled into a ring where wild horses come to scratch themselves against the trunk. The meadow stretches east, south and west, rolling gently over low swells of ground. Beyond the grass the mountains stand grey and close against the sky.
rooms.1803: Poppies grow among the grass here in such numbers that the meadow looks splashed with red paint. The ground rises into a low hummock crowned by an ant hill as large as a beehive, and from its top you can see the grass rolling on and on. The meadow runs east toward a glint of water, south across a shallow dip and west toward a wind-bent thorn. The dry chirring of crickets fills the air.
rooms.1804: The grass grows lush and dark here as the ground slopes toward the Long Lake, and the air smells of water and wet earth. Clumps of rushes rise among the grass, and the soil gives softly underfoot. East, the meadow ends at the lakeshore, where the water glitters beyond a fringe of reeds. The grassland stretches away south and west, and the wind brings the cool breath of the lake across it.
rooms.1805: The meadow comes down to the Long Lake here in a gentle slope of short turf, ending at a narrow beach of grey shingle. The lake stretches away so far that its farther shore is only a faint blue line, and small waves come in with a steady hush. An old rowing boat lies upturned on the shingle, its planks grey and split. The shore runs south among the reeds, and west the long grass of the meadow rises.
rooms.1810: Tall reeds rise from the shallows here, their brown heads nodding over water so still that the sky lies on it unbroken. A path of trodden mud runs along the shore between the reeds and the meadow, printed with the tracks of wading birds and the hooves of horses come down to drink. The shore leads north to a shingle beach and south toward a stand of willows. West, the meadow grass climbs gently away from the water.
rooms.1818: Willows lean far out over the Long Lake here, trailing their long green fronds in the water so that each tree seems to be drinking. Beneath them the shore is a tangle of roots and soft black mud. A small wooden jetty, its posts slimy with weed, runs a few paces out into the lake. The shoreline continues north among the reeds and south toward the edge of a wood, and the meadow lies west.
rooms.1826: The shore curves here, and the first white birches come down almost to the water, their reflections shivering in the small waves. Flat stones along the waterline make good places to sit, and a ring of blackened stones shows where someone has made a fire. North the shore runs on beneath willows, south lies the edge of the woods, and west the meadow grass gives way to a reedy pond. Mist often gathers on the lake here, drifting in over the stones.
rooms.1834: Here the meadow, the lake and the woods all meet. Birches crowd thick to the south, their white trunks bright against the shadows between them, while north the ground slopes down to the shore of the Long Lake. Bracken grows waist-high along the margin of the trees, already turning bronze at its tips. A trail runs west along the edge of the woods. The cool damp of the lake hangs in the air.
rooms.1842: Silver birches stand close together here, their papery bark peeling in white curls and marked with black scars like half-closed eyes. Their small leaves let through a green, flickering light that dances over the ground with every breath of wind. The Birch Woods grow brighter to the north, where they thin toward the lake, and run on south and west in pale ranks. Red-capped toadstools speckled with white grow in clusters among the roots.
rooms.1850: A birch has fallen here and rotted from the inside out, leaving only its tough white bark lying on the ground like a long, hollow pipe. Moss and tiny ferns have taken root along it. The trees around stand close, and the wind in their leaves makes a sound like rain on a roof. Paths lead north, south and west between the white trunks, over leaf litter so thin that the black earth shows through.
rooms.1858: The birches grow in a thick, tangled clump here, many trunks springing from a single great stool where an old tree was coppiced long ago. Beyond them the woods end in a thicket of holly and bramble too dense to pass. The only ways out lie north and west through the white trunks. Bramble runners catch at your ankles, and the blackberries on them are small and sour.
rooms.1857: A ranger's mark has been cut into a birch trunk here, a leaf inside a circle, the cuts darkened and swollen with age. Beneath it a narrow trail runs east and west through the woods, packed hard by careful feet. To the north the trees open a little around a clearing. The bark of the marked tree has healed in thick black ridges around the cuts, like lips closed over a secret.
rooms.1849: A clearing opens among the birches here, floored with soft grass and edged with foxgloves whose purple spires stand taller than a child. A ring of flat stones in the middle holds the ashes of many small fires, swept neat after each one. Paths lead off north, east, south and west between the white trunks. The air is still and warm in the shelter of the trees.
rooms.1841: The birches here are young and slender, growing so close together that their trunks make a pale fence on every side. Their leaves rustle constantly, even when there seems to be no wind at all. North, the trees thin out toward the edge of the woods and the meadow beyond, and paths wind east, south and west among the white stems. Patches of moss glow a vivid green in the dappled light.
rooms.1833: The long grass of the meadow breaks against the woods here like a green sea against a white shore. A single tall birch stands out in the grass ahead of the others, as though it had stepped forward to keep watch. The meadow opens to the north, the Birch Woods begin to the south, and the margin runs east and west between them. Harebells nod on a low bank where the two meet.
rooms.1825: The meadow is broken here by a shallow, reedy pond, where ground water seeps up through the grass and lies still and brown. Yellow flag irises grow along its margin, and the mud around it is pocked with hoofprints. East the land falls away to the lakeshore, south the white wall of the Birch Woods begins, and the meadow runs north and west. The pond smells of mud and crushed rushes.
rooms.1817: Meadowsweet grows in creamy drifts here, its heavy scent rising from the damp ground near the lake. A broken post leans in the grass, the last remnant of a fence that someone once tried to build across the Thrithing. East, willows trail their fronds in the water at the lake's edge, and the meadow runs north, south and west around you. The grass here stays wet with dew long into the day.
rooms.1809: The grass here has been grazed short by wild horses, and the turf is dotted with daisies and clover. A great flat stone lies half sunk in the ground, warm from the sun, with shallow grooves worn into it where generations of shepherds have whetted their knives. East, the meadow slopes to the reedy shore of the Long Lake, and the grass rolls on north, south and west.
rooms.1808: The Meadow Thrithing is at its widest here, a sea of grass that bends and rises in waves under the wind, with nothing to break it but a few clumps of thistle. The sky feels enormous overhead. You can wade through the grass north, east, south or west, and in every direction it looks much the same. Seeds and burrs cling to your clothes at every step.
rooms.1816: An old boundary ditch crosses the meadow here, so overgrown that you see it only when you are about to step into it. Along its bank grows a line of crooked crab-apple trees, their small sour fruit scattered in the grass. The meadow continues north, east, south and west, and the ditch runs off into the grass on either hand. Long ago, someone thought this land was worth dividing.
rooms.1824: The grass grows shorter here as the meadow nears the woods, and bracken has begun to creep out into it in bright green patches. A pair of young birches stand alone in the open like scouts sent ahead of the forest. South, the edge of the woods lies a short walk away, and the meadow spreads north, east and west. The ground is dry and sandy beneath the grass.
rooms.1832: A low bank topped with hazel and blackthorn marks the edge of the woods here, and beyond it the birches crowd together. A narrow gap has been worn through the hedge by the passing of many feet. North lies open meadow, south the Birch Woods, and the bank runs east and west along the margin. Sloes hang dusky blue on the blackthorn, bitter enough to make your mouth pucker.
rooms.1840: Somebody has tapped the birches here for their sap: small wooden spouts have been driven into several trunks, and the bark beneath them is stained dark and sticky. These trees are tall and old, their bark gone rough and grey near the ground. Paths lead north toward the edge of the woods and east, south and west among the white trunks. The air carries the faint, sweet smell of sap.
rooms.1848: The birches give way here to a small stand of dark pines, and the ground beneath them is bare and brown with fallen needles. The change is so abrupt that the light seems to dim, and the air smells of resin instead of grass. Paths lead out of the pines north, east, south and west into the brighter birch woods. Pine cones crunch underfoot.
rooms.1856: A great grey boulder sits among the birches here, as big as a cottage and split down the middle by a crack you could squeeze into. Birch seedlings have rooted in the crack and in every pocket of soil on its top. Trails lead north into a stand of dark pines and east and west through the woods. Moss and lichen paint the boulder in patches of green, grey and orange.
rooms.1855: The birches grow tall and widely spaced here, with soft grass between them and the occasional mossy stump. Their crowns sway far overhead, and the wind among them sounds like the sea. A trail leads north toward a boggy spring, and others run east and west through the white trunks. Through the trees you can make out the grey crag that rises above the Rangers Camp.
rooms.1847: A small spring rises among the birches here and spreads into a boggy patch thick with moss and cotton grass, whose white tufts bob above the green. Someone has laid a line of split logs across the wettest part. Firmer ground leads north, east, south and west around the bog. The water is brown with peat but cold and clean.
rooms.1839: Bracken grows shoulder-high between the birches here, its newest fronds still unrolling from tight brown fists. A path has been beaten through it, winding north toward the edge of the woods and dividing to run east, south and west. The bracken hides the ground completely, and the path feels close and green. Webs strung between the fronds glitter with dew.
rooms.1831: Wild raspberry canes crowd the margin of the woods here, a thorny tangle between the meadow grass and the first birches. An old woodcutter's stack of birch logs, grey and furred with moss, sits at the edge of the trees. The meadow lies north, the woods south, and the margin runs east and west. The logs have lain here so long that saplings grow from them.
rooms.1823: A ring of grey standing stones, none taller than your waist, stands half hidden in the grass here. Lichen has crusted them yellow and white, and the grass inside the ring grows shorter and greener than the meadow around it. The meadow stretches north, east and west, and south the woods begin. No one has ever moved these stones, though the Thrithing has been grazed and crossed for longer than anyone remembers.
rooms.1815: The meadow dips here into a shallow bowl, sheltered from the wind, where the grass grows lush and tall and the air lies warm and still. Wild horses have rolled here, leaving round, flattened patches in the grass. The ground rises gently again to the north, east, south and west. Cornflowers grow in the bottom of the bowl, as blue as a summer sky.
rooms.1807: A ruined shepherd's hut stands in the grass here, little more than a ring of knee-high stone walls with a gap for a doorway. Nettles fill the inside. The meadow spreads around it, rolling north toward a wind-bent thorn and away east, south and west. The mountains loom closer here, their lower slopes dark with heather.
rooms.1806: The Meadow Thrithing opens here beside the end of the plains road, which lies just west across a strip of stony ground. Wheel ruts and hoof marks have pressed a faint track into the grass, fading as it heads out into the meadow. The grass runs north toward the mountain slopes, and east and south it rolls away in long silver swells. The wind smells of grass and distant rain.
rooms.1814: A great old oak stands alone in the meadow here, its crown spreading wide over a circle of shade where the grass grows thin. Its lowest branch has been worn smooth by generations of herders sitting on it, and initials are cut deep into the bark of the trunk. The meadow stretches north, east, south and west from the shade of the oak. Acorns crunch underfoot.
rooms.1822: A stream winds through the meadow here in a channel cut deep into the soft earth, so hidden by overhanging grass that you hear it before you see it. A flat stone has been laid across it as a bridge. The meadow continues north, east and west, and south it runs down to the edge of the woods. Watercress grows thick in the clear, slow water.
rooms.1830: The stream from the meadow runs into the woods here, slipping under a bank of roots and vanishing among the birches. Kingcups grow bright yellow along its edge, and the ground is soft and wet. North lies the open meadow, south the white trunks of the Birch Woods, and the margin of the trees runs east and west. The air is cool and smells of wet moss.
rooms.1838: The stream from the meadow wanders through the birches here in a bed of brown pebbles, and the trees lean over it from both banks. Moss and ferns grow thick along the water, and a fallen trunk makes a bridge across it. Paths lead north toward the edge of the woods and east, south and west through the trees. The water chuckles softly over the stones.
rooms.1846: Here the stream spreads into a small, clear pool among the birches, its surface spotted with fallen leaves. Reflections of the white trunks shiver in it whenever the wind stirs. The pool drains away under a bank of roots, and paths lead north, east, south and west around it. A flat stone has been set at the water's edge, worn smooth by the knees of rangers filling their water skins.
rooms.1854: The smell of woodsmoke drifts through the birches here from the Rangers Camp just to the west, and the ground is trodden bare along a well-used path. Several of the trunks have been notched with the rangers' leaf mark. The path leads west to the camp, while other trails run north toward a woodland pool and east deeper into the woods. The crag that rises behind the camp shows grey through the leaves.
rooms.1853: The rangers of the Long Lake have made their camp in a clearing among the birches, at the foot of a grey crag that rises sheer above the trees. Lean-tos of birch poles and bark stand around a large fire pit ringed with stones, and racks for drying hides and fish stand nearby. A rope ladder hangs down the face of the crag, and above it a narrow path climbs up the mountain. Trails lead north, east and west into the woods.
rooms.1845: The birches have been thinned here by careful cutting, the stumps cut clean and low, and stacks of poles lie seasoning in neat piles. The Rangers Camp lies just to the south, and the crackle of its fire carries through the trees. Trails lead north, east and west through the woods. The ground is covered with fresh chips of white wood.
rooms.1837: Old birches with thick, rough-barked trunks stand here, their branches hung with long grey lichen that sways like an old man's beard. The ground beneath is soft with fallen leaves and the crumbled remains of dead branches. Paths lead north to the edge of the woods, south toward a place of cut stumps and stacked poles, and east and west among the trees. It is quieter here than in the rest of the woods.
rooms.1829: A hunting blind of woven birch branches has been built low among the bracken at the edge of the woods here, facing out over the meadow where the horses graze. It is cleverly made and hard to spot until you are almost on top of it. North lies the open grass, south the Birch Woods, and the margin runs east and west. The bracken around it has been carefully left uncut.
rooms.1821: Molehills scatter the meadow here in dozens of small brown heaps, and the grass between them is short and patchy. A crooked wild pear tree stands among them, heavy with small hard fruit. The meadow runs north toward the end of the plains road, east toward a hidden stream and west across open grass, while south the edge of the woods lies close. The soil turned up by the moles is dark and rich.
rooms.1813: The meadow runs right up to the end of the plains road here, and the road's stony bank lies just to the north, thick with gorse. Cart ruts run a little way into the grass and stop. The long grass stretches east toward a lone oak and south across the open land, and west it follows the line of the old road. The yellow gorse flowers give off a sweet, nutty smell in the warmth.
rooms.1812: The blackened walls of Townsbridge's ruined coaching inn stand just to the north, where the road through the plains passes beneath its arch, and the meadow grass has crept right up to the soot-stained stones. Nettles and willowherb grow thick along the foot of the walls. The meadow runs east, south and west. Even the wind seems to shun the ruin, and the grass near it barely stirs.
rooms.1820: A burnt-out hay wagon lies on its side in the grass here, its wheels charred to their iron rims and its bed long since rotted through. Brambles have grown up through the wreck and hold it in a thorny embrace. The meadow stretches north toward the ruins of Townsbridge, east and west across the grass, and south to the edge of the woods. Rosehips glow red among the brambles.
rooms.1828: The edge of the woods here is a tangle of elder and dog rose, with the white birches rising behind. Elderflowers hang in creamy plates, filling the air with a heavy sweetness. A gap in the tangle leads south into the woods, while north the meadow opens out and the margin runs east and west. A few charred fence posts still stand in the grass, the remains of an old field boundary.
rooms.1836: Birch polypores bulge from many of the trunks here like grey-white shelves, and one dead tree is so crowded with them that it looks like a stack of plates. The woods are dim and quiet, the canopy thick overhead. Paths lead north to the edge of the woods and east, south and west deeper among the trees. The smell of damp wood and fungus is strong.
rooms.1844: An old charcoal burners' hearth lies here among the birches, a round patch of black earth where nothing grows. The rangers use the cleared ground for archery, and a straw target hangs from a branch at the far side, bristling with old arrow holes. Paths lead north, east, south and west. Woodsmoke from the camp drifts through the trees.
rooms.1852: A well-trodden path leads east from here into the Rangers Camp, where a fire burns in a ring of stones beneath the grey crag. Birch branches have been cut and laid along the path's muddiest stretches. North lies a patch of blackened earth where charcoal was once burned, and west the woods grow thicker. The smell of woodsmoke and cooking drifts from the camp.
rooms.1851: The Birch Woods end against a steep rocky bank here, its face hung with ferns and dripping with water from a spring somewhere above. The water collects in a basin of moss at the foot of the bank before trickling away. Ways lead north and east through the trees. The rock is cold and slick, and green with liverwort.
rooms.1843: The birches grow in a long line here along the top of an old earth bank, as though they had been planted as a hedge long ago and left to grow wild. Their roots grip the bank like knotted fingers. Paths lead north, east and south along and through the line of trees. Below the bank the ground is soft and deep with dead leaves.
rooms.1835: The Birch Woods begin here on the edge of the open plains, which stretch away west under a wide sky, flat and grey-green. A few birches have strayed out into the grass, small and stunted by the wind. The woods run east and south, and north lies the margin of the meadow. Underfoot, the plains grass and the woodland leaves mingle.
rooms.1827: The meadow, the woods and the plains meet here in a broad corner of rough grass. West, the plains stretch away toward the ruins of Townsbridge, whose broken gables can just be seen. The birches begin to the south, the meadow lies north, and the margin of the woods runs east. A boundary stone, leaning and half buried, marks some old division of the land.
rooms.1819: The meadow ends here where the plains begin, and the difference is easy to see: the lush grass of the Thrithing gives way west to shorter, sparser growth and patches of bare earth. Old plough ridges still show beneath the plains grass, the remains of Townsbridge's fields. The meadow runs north, east and south. Thistles stand in ragged ranks along the boundary.
rooms.1811: The meadow's edge lies close to the ruins of Townsbridge here: the road passes beneath the burnt arch of the old coaching inn just to the north, and west stands the shell of a great barn with its wall fallen open to the grass. The long grass grows thick around the scattered stones. The meadow runs east and south, away from the ruins. A smell of old ash lingers on the air.
rooms.8186: This was once Townsbridge's great barn, and its stone walls still stand to the eaves, though the roof has fallen in at one end and its timbers lie blackened across the floor. The east wall has collapsed outward, opening the barn to the long grass of the meadow. A doorway north leads to the road through the village, and others open south and west onto the plains. Charred grain lies drifted in the corners, black and hard as gravel.
rooms.8187: A scarecrow's cross stands crooked in an abandoned field here, its rags long since rotted away, its arms still spread as if to warn off birds that stopped coming years ago. Coarse grass and docks have swallowed the crop rows. North rise the walls of a burnt barn, east the lush grass of the meadow begins, and the plains run south and west. The wind moves through the grass with a dry, whispering sound.
rooms.8188: A rusted plough lies abandoned in the grass here, its share still buried in the earth where it stopped mid-furrow, as though the ploughman simply walked away. Grass has grown up through its frame. East the land rises to the edge of the woods, and the plains stretch north, south and west. Yarrow and ragwort grow everywhere, the flowers of land that no one tends.
rooms.8189: The plains meet the birch woods here, and the first white trunks stand just to the east, bright against the grey-green grass. A sheepfold of piled stones has half collapsed nearby, its gate gone and its walls sliding into the turf. The plains stretch north and west, empty and quiet. The grass here is short and tough, cropped close by the wind.
rooms.8185: An old well stands alone in the open here, its stone ring still sound but its windlass gone and its little roof fallen in. A dropped pebble falls a long way before a faint splash comes back up. Whatever farmstead once stood beside it has vanished, leaving only the well. The plains run north, east, south and west around it, flat and windswept.
rooms.8184: The plains are flat and featureless here, the grass beaten down along a faint trail that runs from the ruined village toward the south. A sour, rotten smell drifts on the wind from somewhere close by, and a few small bones lie bleached among the thistles. The plains continue north toward the ruins, east toward an abandoned field and west across empty grass. Nothing grows here taller than your knee.
rooms.8183: This is the back of Townsbridge, where the gardens and yards of the village once ran down to the fields. North stands the blackened shell of a burnt shop, and east the walls of a great barn. West the ground falls away toward a pit, and the stench rising from it is enough to make your eyes water. The plains run south, open and empty under the sky.
rooms.15066: The road leaves Garathorm through the Eastern Gatehouse, whose grey towers rise just to the west, and runs out across the plains toward the ruins of Townsbridge. A weathered sign stands at the roadside. East, the road leads to the blackened shell of a burnt shop, the first building of the dead village. South, a track leads to a pit from which a foul smell drifts. Wildflowers bloom along the verges as though nothing were wrong.
rooms.8150: Low, grassy mounds lie in rows here, each about the length of a man, with nothing to mark them but an occasional stick driven into the earth. These are older graves than those in the pit to the north, dug with more care and long since grown over. The plains run east from here, flat and empty. Even on the brightest day the place feels cold.
rooms.8181: This small cottage stood closest to the road, and though its thatch is gone, a few charred rafters still span the walls and a lean-to of rotten planks shelters one corner. A table lies overturned there beside a broken spinning wheel. The doorway north opens onto the road, and a gap in the east wall looks out toward the pit, from which a dreadful smell drifts in. The walls are scored with long scratches that no tool made.
rooms.15070: The vaulted passage of the Eastern Gatehouse runs through the thickness of the outer wall, lit by lanterns in iron cages and cold even on the warmest day. Great oak gates stand open at either end, west to the Trade Road and east to the road across the plains. Two lesser doors in the side walls are barred with heavy timbers: the north one is painted with faded stars and tumbling clowns, and the south one bears the worn crest of an academy. The flagstones are rutted deep by cartwheels.
rooms.9722: The Trade Road ends its run through the outer town here at the Eastern Gatehouse, whose squat towers loom just to the east. This is a busy crossing: Esh Road leads north between tall merchant houses, Pasocaoa Boulevard opens broad and straight to the south, and the Trade Road itself stretches back west toward the inner city. A long stone trough for watering horses stands beside the gate, and the cobbles around it are never quite dry.
rooms.9749: Esh Road leaves the bustle of the Trade Road here and runs north between tall houses of timber and pale plaster, their upper floors jutting out on carved brackets until they nearly meet overhead. Painted shutters in red and saffron hang open beside the windows. The street is paved with small, close-set cobbles laid in sweeping fan patterns. South, the clamour of the gatehouse crossing carries up the street.
rooms.9748: The smell of spices hangs thick in the air here, pouring from the open doors of a long warehouse where sacks are stacked to the rafters: pepper, cinnamon, cloves and stranger things from lands beyond the desert. A brass weighing beam hangs above the doorway. The road runs on north toward the trading post and south toward the Trade Road. The gutter beside the cobbles is stained yellow with spilled saffron.
rooms.9799: A broad doorway in a building of honey-coloured stone opens west into the Trading Post, its lintel carved with a pair of scales, a camel and a ship under sail. Iron hitching rails line the street outside, polished by countless reins. Esh Road continues north past a row of tiny shopfronts and south toward the spice warehouses. The cobbles here are worn smooth by the passage of handcarts.
rooms.9798: Little shops crowd both sides of the street here, none wider than a doorway: a moneychanger's booth with a barred window, a seller of inks and fine paper, a maker of brass lamps whose wares hang glinting in clusters from the eaves. Strings of paper lanterns are slung across the street from balcony to balcony. Esh Road runs north to a corner and south toward the trading post.
rooms.9797: Esh Road turns a corner here, and in the angle of the wall stands a small shrine: a niche holding a squat bronze figure with a round belly and a contented smile. Offerings of rice and marigolds are heaped at his feet, and his belly has been rubbed bright by passing hands. The road leads south toward the little shops and west between tall, quiet houses. A smell of incense lingers about the niche.
rooms.9796: A neat house with a green-painted door and a little courtyard garden stands on the south side of the street here, its gate hung with a small brass bell. Pots of herbs and bright flowers line its windowsills. Esh Road runs east to a corner shrine and west along a row of tall houses. The street is quieter here, away from the warehouses, and swept clean every morning.
rooms.9747: This snug home belongs to a family of merchants, and their trade shows in every corner: a rug woven with birds and vines covers the floor, lacquered chests stand against the walls, and a brass lamp of fine filigree hangs from a beam, scattering tiny points of light. Low cushions surround a table barely a foot high. The air smells of sandalwood and tea. The green door north leads back out to Esh Road.
rooms.9795: A public well stands in a small square here, its stone curb worn hollow by ropes and its pulley sheltered under a little tiled roof with upturned eaves. Benches around it make a meeting place for the neighbourhood. Esh Road runs east toward a house with a green door and west past more tall houses. Children have chalked games of hops and squares on the cobbles around the well.
rooms.9794: A tall, narrow house with a carved balcony stands on the north side of the street here, its door painted with a pair of golden fish swimming in a circle. Wind chimes of thin brass hang from its eaves and ring softly in every breeze. Esh Road leads east toward a public well and west toward the Trade Road. Lanterns on tall poles line the street.
rooms.9746: The ground floor of this narrow house is a single long room, cool and dim behind closed shutters, with a floor of red tiles and walls hung with painted silk. A shrine shelf holds a few small figures and a dish of grey incense ash. A cushioned bench runs beneath a row of empty birdcages of delicate bamboo. The door south, painted with golden fish, opens back onto Esh Road.
rooms.9793: Esh Road begins here, branching off the Trade Road past a row of solid counting-houses whose iron-bound doors and barred windows speak of the money kept inside. Brass plates beside each door bear the names of merchant houses in several scripts. West, the Trade Road bustles in the shadow of the inner city's wall. Esh Road runs east toward a street of tall houses and swaying lanterns.

1346.description: The leaf is carved with such care that every vein shows, and beneath it runs a line of flowing elven script, too weathered to read. The stone is faintly warm to the touch, even in shadow.

1321.description: The gate is not forged but grown, a lattice of thin silver-barked branches woven so tightly that not even a hand will pass. A leaf-shaped hollow at its centre looks as though it waits for a key that is not made of iron.

1318.description: The figure is plainly elven, tall and fine-boned, her hair bound back with a circlet of leaves. Words are cut into the base in a flowing script, and a patient scholar might make them out as THE LIGHT REMEMBERS.

1338.description: The rune is a simple shape, a straight line crossed by a curve like a drawn bow, and the gold in its grooves is not paint but sap that has dried hard and bright. Elves set such stones to mark the ways to their trees.

8657.description: Thousands of tiny stones make up the sun, each set by hand. Its rays point down every path that leaves this place, and one ray, longer than the rest, points toward a part of the forest where no path runs at all.

8267.description: It is the stonemason to the life, from his heavy jaw to the chip of granite caught in his beard, carved with a great deal of affection and not a little malice.

8260.description: Each jar is marked with a scratched symbol rather than a word: a leaf, a moon, an eye, a drop of water. One, set apart on a high shelf, is marked with a skull and sealed with black wax.

8218.description: The tankards bear scratched names and signs: a plough, a horseshoe, a fish, a pair of dice. One hook has a black ribbon tied around it, and no tankard hangs there.

8501.description: Scraping away the lichen reveals the word GARATHORM and a number too worn to read. On the other face, cut much more recently, is a leaf inside a circle, the mark the rangers of the Long Lake use to show the way to their camp.

8505.description: Every stone in the cairn was carried up by a climber, and many bear scratched initials or tiny charms tied on with string. It is said to bring luck to add a stone before the climb.

1823.description: There are nine stones, each marked on its inner face with a faint spiral. Shepherds say the ring is older than Garathorm, and that a foal born inside it will never be taken by wolves.

1853.description: A deerskin stretched on a frame has been painted with a map of the country around: the meadow, the lake, the birch woods and the road to Townsbridge. Red marks show where bears and wolves have been seen, and a black cross has been drawn over the burnt village.

15066.description: The sign reads TOWNSBRIDGE, with an arrow pointing down the road. Someone has painted a crude skull over the name, and beneath it, in smaller and shakier letters, TURN BACK.

9797.description: The bronze figure is a god of trade and good fortune to the merchants who built these streets, and it is thought lucky to rub his belly before striking a bargain. A small brass plate beneath him reads HONEST WEIGHT, HONEST WORD.

creatures.long_desc: A golden stag stands among the trees, light gathering in the tines of its antlers.
creatures.description: The stag's coat is the warm colour of the forest's leaves, and its antlers branch wide and high with a faint gilt sheen along every tine. It holds its head proudly and watches you with large dark eyes, more curious than afraid. The elves are said to count the killing of one of these beasts a grave offence.

creatures.long_desc: A giant black spider waits in a sagging web strung across the edge of the light.
creatures.description: Its body is as large as a hound's, covered in coarse black hair, and its eight long legs are banded with dull red. A cluster of glassy eyes catches the golden light as it shifts its weight on the web. These spiders creep out of the Old Forest to hunt along its border, though they never venture far into the radiant wood.
rooms: At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest
The Edge Of The Radiant Forest
A Corner In The Radiant Forest

creatures.long_desc: A dun wild horse grazes in the long grass, swishing its black tail at the flies.
creatures.description: A sturdy, short-legged horse with a dun coat, a black mane that has never known a comb and a dark stripe along its spine. It lifts its head to watch you, ears pricked, ready to wheel away across the meadow with the rest of its herd. The horses of the Thrithing have run wild here for longer than anyone remembers.

creatures.long_desc: A shaggy brown bear rears up against a birch, raking the white bark with its claws.
creatures.description: A huge brown bear with a hump of muscle across its shoulders and a coat ragged with burrs and twigs. Its muzzle is sticky with honey from some raided hive, and its small eyes regard you with short-tempered suspicion. Risen on its hind legs, it stands taller than any man.

creatures.long_desc: A furtive poacher crouches over a snare in the undergrowth, skinning knife in hand.
creatures.description: A lean, hollow-cheeked man in a patched jerkin of greasy leather, with a game bag slung across his back and a coil of snare wire at his belt. He has the darting eyes of someone who knows the rangers are never far away, and he will fight like a cornered weasel rather than be taken. Feathers and tufts of fur cling to his sleeves.
rooms: At The Edge Of The Woods

creatures.long_desc: An ash-grey wraith drifts through the ruins, trailing a thin smell of old smoke.
creatures.description: It has the shape of a villager wrapped in a long, tattered shroud, but the whole of it is made of drifting ash and smoke that never quite settles. Where its face should be there are only two embers, dull red and full of grief and hatred. It is one of the dead of Townsbridge, who perished when the village burned and cannot rest.

creatures.short_desc: a ranger of the Long Lake
creatures.long_desc: A ranger of the Long Lake keeps watch here, leaning on an unstrung longbow.
creatures.description: A weathered woman in mottled green and brown, with a quiver at her hip and a silver leaf pinned at the throat of her cloak. Her face is brown and lined from years of wind and weather, and her grey eyes miss nothing that moves in the grass. The rangers keep the meadow and the woods around the Long Lake safe, and ask little in return.
rooms: By The Shore Of The Long Lake

creatures.short_desc: a watchman of the outer town
creatures.long_desc: A watchman of the outer town strolls by, his lantern pole resting on one shoulder.
creatures.description: A thickset, good-humoured man in a quilted coat dyed the blue of the town watch, with a short club at his belt and a lantern on a pole for the night rounds. He knows every merchant on the street by name, and most of their debts as well. His boots are worn down at the heels from years of walking the same cobbles.

items.room_desc: A stag's antler with a faint golden sheen lies here.
items.description: A long, many-tined antler from one of the stags of the Radiant Forest. Its surface has a faint golden sheen that catches the light like old gilt, and carvers in Garathorm pay well for such antlers to make handles and charms.

items.short_desc: a skein of glimmering spider silk
items.room_desc: A skein of grey spider silk lies here, glimmering faintly.
items.description: A loose skein of spider silk wound around a twig, still a little sticky at one end. Where it has hung in the light of the Radiant Forest it has taken on a faint golden glimmer, and weavers prize it for the finest thread.

items.room_desc: A short skinning knife with a hooked tip lies here.
items.description: A short, heavy-backed knife with a hooked tip for opening hides, its bone handle wrapped in strips of rabbit skin. The blade has been sharpened so often that it has worn thin and wickedly keen.

items.room_desc: A tarnished silver locket on a thin chain lies here.
items.description: A small silver locket, black with tarnish and warped by heat, on a chain mended with a twist of wire. Inside is a tiny painted portrait of a smiling family, and TOWNSBRIDGE is engraved on the back in careful letters. It is always cold to the touch.

items.room_desc: A broken slab of wild honeycomb lies here, oozing gold.
items.description: A ragged slab of honeycomb torn from a wild hive in some hollow birch, heavy and dripping with dark honey. It is sticky, sweet and very filling.
